name: Parmashta
title: Son of Haman
summary: Parmashta was one of the ten sons of Haman, the Agagite, who was an enemy of the Jewish people in the Persian Empire. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies following King Ahasuerus' decree, and his name was hung on the gallows together with the other sons.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Plot Against the Jews
keyEvents.description: Haman, son of Hammedatha, planned the extermination of all Jews in the Persian Empire, which directly affected the fate of the entire family.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Downfall
keyEvents.description: After Queen Esther revealed Haman's evil plan to King Ahasuerus, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' Victory and the Killing of Haman's Sons
keyEvents.description: Parmashta was killed along with his nine brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Sons Hanged
keyEvents.description: At Queen Esther's request, King Ahasuerus ordered that Haman's ten sons, including Parmashta, be hanged on gallows as a public demonstration.

keyEvents.title: The Feast of Purim Established
keyEvents.description: The victory over Haman and his sons, including Parmashta, became the basis for the annual feast of Purim, which Jews celebrate to commemorate their deliverance.
